deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematics. It is an archival wrapper or folder sheet. In faint pencil it carries a short contents list for the bundle of loose sheets that follows. The hand is probably a later editor or archivist, not Riemann. Candidates are Dedekind, H. Weber or a librarian, but I cannot attribute the hand with certainty. The previous page (45r) is the matching title: 'Nachlass Riemann's: Mathematisches, Physikalisches. 45'. The list reads:
(1) 'Anziehung (und Bewegung) des Ellipsoids': the attraction (and motion) of an ellipsoid. This presumably points to material connected with Riemann's 1861 paper 'Ein Beitrag zu den Untersuchungen über die Bewegung eines flüssigen gleichartigen Ellipsoides' (Abh. Ges. Wiss. Göttingen 9, 1861). It may also point to potential-theoretic notes on the gravitational attraction of a homogeneous ellipsoid.
(2) 'Scheint zum Theil zu der Arbeit über Nobili'sche Ringe zu gehören': this seems partly to belong to the work on Nobili's rings. That is Riemann's 'Zur Theorie der Nobili'schen Farbenringe' (Ann. Phys. Chem. 95, 1855).
(3) 'Wärme im Ellipsoid': heat (conduction) in an ellipsoid.
(4) '?': an unidentified group.
The following page (46r) opens with computations on u'' + q^2 u = 0 and on u'' + x u = 0 (Airy/Stokes-type equation). It contains integral representations with x^3/y in the exponent and a Riccati substitution v^2 + v' = x. It also tries a WKB-like ansatz u = phi(x) cos(alpha x^{3/2}). These may correspond to the editor's item 4 or to one of the physical topics. None of that is on this page, so there is nothing to reconstruct here.

results.what: Editorial contents list of the bundle: attraction/motion of an ellipsoid; material possibly belonging to the Nobili rings paper; heat in an ellipsoid; an unidentified item

deep.surprise_reason: The page is only a later archival or editorial table of contents. The topics it names (fluid ellipsoid motion, 1861; Nobili rings, 1855) are Riemann's published and well-known works. There is no mathematics on it.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'Nobilische[?]' should read 'Nobili'sche' (Nobili's rings, cf. Riemann 1855). 'Scheint' and 'gehören' are correct.
The hand appears to be an editor's or archivist's pencil note, not Riemann's own writing; this is likely but not certain.
